title: Mitred square — two colour
subtitle: A diagonal colour split across the mitred construction, worked in DK cotton
excerpt: Two colours meet at the central decrease spine of the mitred square, producing a clean diagonal split from corner to corner. Colour A works the first half of each row; colour B takes over at the midpoint. The yarn change sits invisibly inside the decrease stitch.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 2 (1887), diagonal square chapter (Internet Archive). The two-colour construction is a standard colourwork adaptation of the single-colour mitred square.
heroPrompt: A two-colour mitred crochet square in sage green and cream DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. A clean diagonal stripe runs corner to corner, the square 10 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished square measures 10 × 10 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Mitred square — two colour
chartDefinition.caption: Colour A (grey) fills the left half of each row; colour B (cream) fills the right half. The colour change happens inside the dc2tog at the centre.

glossaryTerms.definition: To change colour mid-stitch: work the dc until the final pull-through, drop the current yarn, pick up the new colour, and draw it through the remaining two loops. The new colour appears from the next stitch onward.
Double crochet two together: insert hook, pull up a loop, insert hook in next stitch, pull up a loop, yarn over and draw through all three loops. One stitch decreased.

content.text: The two-colour mitred square splits colour A and colour B at the central decrease, giving a diagonal stripe that runs from the top corner to the bottom corner. The
sits inside the dc2tog at the midpoint of every row so the join is invisible from the right side.

Use two separate yarn balls or butterflies, one per colour. Carry the unused colour loosely along the wrong side between the midpoint and the edge, or simply cut and rejoin each row for a cleaner back. The second approach uses slightly more yarn but eliminates any carried-yarn distortion.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 5 g each of two DK-weight cotton colours (colour A and colour B). A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Colour A: dc in 2nd ch from hook, dc in next 8 ch. Work dc2tog over next 2 ch, changing to colour B on the final pull-through of the
. Colour B: dc in each remaining 9 ch. Turn. (19 sts.)
Ch 1 with current colour. Continue in established stripe, changing colour at the dc2tog midpoint on each row. Two stitches decrease per row.
Dc2tog over final 2 sts. Fasten off. (1 st.)
For a three-stripe diagonal, try the striped mitred square, which changes colour every two rows. Or work a log cabin square for a different approach to colourwork in rows.
